entries.group: owed's second set is a comprehension over unapproved(data), which is empty whenever L417 runs
entries.grounds: L417 is `owed = {(cid,rid) for cid in exposed ...} | {(r['contract'], r['requirement']) for r in unapproved(data)}`; the mutant makes the second element `{(r['requirement'],) for r in unapproved(data)}`. PROOF the second comprehension is always over []: to reach L417 every contract in data['contracts'] must have compiled at L386 `current[c.id]=compile_spec(c,...,approvals=approvals,...)`; compile_spec (aisef2/product/compiler.py:60-61) calls require_approved first (aisef2/product/approval.py:82-96), which raises UnapprovedContract -- a ContractError, and ContractError(ValueError) (aisef2/product/contract.py:26) -- when any requirement a contract cites has no approval binding both current hashes; the except at L387 catches ValueError and re-raises MigrationError 'contract <id> does not compile' at L388. unapproved(data) (L602-613) returns the (contract,requirement) pairs with no binding approval using the identical predicate `not any(not binding_problems(a,r,c) ...)` over the same data['contracts'], data['requirements'] and data['approvals']. So unapproved(data) is non-empty IFF some contract failed require_approved IFF migrate already raised at L388; therefore at L417 unapproved(data)==[]. Measured: len(unapproved(data))==0 for LedgerLock 2.0.0 (59/59 approved), era_bundle() and the A03 fixture. The empty comprehension yields the empty set for both the original and the mutant, so owed is identical; the mutated element expression is never evaluated. Mutant SURVIVED the 5 kill files.

entries.group: the L418 self-consistency guard: both disjuncts are held False by the construction above it on every reachable bundle, so weakening or->and is unobservable
entries.grounds: Changes the guard `if lacks != owed or len(candidate['approvals'])+len(withheld) != len(data['approvals'])` to `... and ...`. This is a defensive self-check that migrate's own bookkeeping reconciled; on valid input both disjuncts are False (so or and and agree). Disjunct A (lacks != owed): by the [103] proof unapproved(data)==[] at L417, so owed = {exposed contracts x their requirement_ids}; lacks = unapproved(candidate) which, by construction (candidate drops exactly the withheld approvals, whose contracts are the exposed/unbound ones), equals owed -- A is False. Disjunct B (count): candidate['approvals'] = [a for a in data['approvals'] if _key(a) not in dropped] and withheld iterates the full approvals tuple, so each withheld approval both removes its data approval and is counted -- B is False; measured on a crafted duplicate-approval bundle (an identical second approval of a withheld contract), migrate did NOT raise even in the ORIGINAL (withheld counted the duplicate, candidate dropped both: 2 kept + 7 withheld == 9 = len(data)), so duplicates do not make B fire. The mutant differs from the original only when exactly one disjunct is True, which requires migrate's construction to be internally inconsistent -- a state no shape-valid, kernel-loadable, all-contracts-compiled, plan-rebound bundle produces. Not provably EQUIVALENT (the two disjuncts guard independent failure modes and are not identically-valued by a single code fact), so AUDITED.
